Guide Planning Your Compartments How to work out how many lockers you need, what sizes to order and where to place them, using simple numbers from your own site. ⬇ Download PDF All resources 📐 1. Estimate peak demand Size the bank for the busiest day, not the average one. Count how many people use the space, how many items arrive or are stored at peak and how long each item stays. Number of users on a peak day Items per user at the same time Average time an item stays in a locker Seasonal peaks such as festivals or exam weeks 📐 2. Choose the size mix Most sites need a blend of compartment sizes. Measure the typical items you will store and add a few extra-large compartments for bulky exceptions. Small: documents, keys, phones Medium: bags, laptops, small parcels Large: backpacks, cartons, equipment 📐 3. Add a buffer Plan for about 15 to 20 percent more compartments than your peak figure so that people are never turned away and maintenance can take a unit out of service. 📐 4. Pick the right location Place lockers where people already walk, close to entrances or lifts, in view of cameras or staff and away from damp or heat.
